summary.headline: Pyramid Technoplast Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14% YoY to ₹196 crore and PAT rose 52%, with EBITDA up 68% to ₹20 crore and FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.6%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹196 crore (+14% YoY) and FY26 revenue of ₹684 crore (+15%), with Q4 gross profit up 33% to ₹56 crore and EBITDA up 68% to ₹20 crore. FY26 PAT was ₹29 crore (4.2% margin) and EBITDA margin improved to 8.6% from 7.9%. Installed capacity rose 22% YoY to 76,931 MTPA after the major expansion phase, with utilisation around 69% in the quarter. Management said the major capex cycle is largely complete, with only about ₹20 crore of maintenance and balance capex planned for FY27. Q4 gains were helped by inventory bought at lower prices before a sharp rise in raw material costs.

segments.name: MS Drums
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 29% YoY on 35% volume growth. WADA plant MS drum utilisation was about 51%.

segments.name: HDPE Drums
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 20% YoY on 8% volume growth. WADA plant HDPE drum utilisation was about 72%.

segments.name: IBC
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 5% YoY with 6% volume growth. IBC share of revenue rose to 41% in FY26 from 34%. WADA plant IBC utilisation was about 68%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of around ₹800 crore, per management in Q&A.
FY27 EBITDA expected in the ₹75-80 crore range, per management; management also said margins should stay in double digits.
Capacity utilisation expected to move toward 80% in FY27; IBC and polymer drum utilisation seen reaching 70-75% within 3-6 months.
Solar project cuts annual power cost by about ₹15 crore at full run-rate, with about ₹10-12 crore in the first year; ₹3 crore subsidy not yet provisioned.
Recycling plant (5,000 MTPA) expected to meet 10-12% of raw metal needs, with licence expected June-July 2026 and annual savings of at least ₹5 crore.
Employee cost expected to stay at about ₹7-7.25 crore per quarter.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity up 22% YoY to 76,931 MTPA; utilisation about 69% in Q4, targeted to reach about 80% in FY27.
FY27 maintenance and balance capex about ₹20 crore; new capex only if demand or a new project requires it.
WADA plant fully operational across IBC, HDPE and MS drums; phase 1 revenue potential about ₹200 crore, with phase 2 infrastructure built for up to ₹400 crore by adding machines.
Solar: 6 MW commissioned in Gujarat on Oct 30, 2025; 5 MW Baruch and 2.25 MW Maharashtra commissioned Feb 2, 2026; 1 MW Baruch pending. Total investment about ₹60 crore.
Recycling plant processed about 200 MT in the quarter during trial; awaiting final PCB licence expected June-July 2026. Capex about ₹10-12 crore.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as fine and said price increases are being passed through, with transport cost pass-through taking 15-20 days to a month.
Raw material prices rose about ₹50 per kg; management said inventory held before the increase generated gains that will flow into Q1 FY27.
Inventory days cut to about 25-30 days from about 45 days because imports stopped and material is now bought locally; HDPE rate around ₹150-160/kg.
Management cited about 40% domestic IBC market share and said quality and technology act as entry barriers.
Management expects the FY27 product mix to be about 45% IBC, 45% polymer drums and 10-12% MS drums.

qa_highlights.question: Is the solar plant fully commissioned and is guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: 1 MW remains to be commissioned; benefit about ₹10 crore this year rising to about ₹15 crore next year. Guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin came from inventory gains, and is the 45-day inventory strategy still in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains fell in Q4 and will show up in Q1. Inventory has been cut to 25-30 days because imports have stopped; conversion cost rose to about ₹25/kg from ₹20/kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and repayment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Term loan repayment has started and debt is expected to be repaid over 3-4 years. Short-term borrowing rose to ₹8-10 crore, mainly due to local purchases replacing imports.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IBC and polymer segment mix change, and what are the utilisation peaks?
qa_highlights.answer: IBC and polymer drum utilisation are expected to reach 70-75% within 3-6 months. IBC is 41% of FY26 revenue versus 34% last year and is not expected to jump to 60-70%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recycling plant's potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Licence expected in 1-2 months; savings of at least ₹5 crore a year on 5,000 MT, from avoiding middlemen at ₹10-15/kg lower cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue target is around ₹800 crore.

risks_watch: Raw material is largely imported polymer, now sourced locally at higher cost; the company says quality is unchanged, but management wording on quality was inconsistent in Q&A.
Inventory holding of 25-30 days exposes the company to price declines; management says losses would be limited.
Short-term borrowing rose to ₹8-10 crore; interest cost was described by an analyst as about 30% of PAT.
Recycling licence timing (June-July 2026) is a key dependency for the margin benefit.
Diesel price and logistics costs: the company owns trucks and passes cost increases through with a lag of 15-20 days to a month.
Solar subsidy of ₹3 crore not yet provisioned; timing depends on certificate issuance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the outlook, with the operating story emphasised. Answers were loose and often repetitive on inventory, margins and the recycling benefit, and some figures were given approximately or revised during the call (for example the debt repayment horizon and the EBITDA range).
key_quotes: So our installed production capacity increased 22% year-on-year to 76,931 metric ton per annum, reflecting successful execution of our expansion strategy.
With the completion of this expansion phase, our major CAPEX cycle is now largely behind us and we expect only around 20 crore of maintenance and balance CAPEX during financial year 27.
There is no compromise on quality.

adds.what: Recycling plant 5,000 MTPA (metal recycling, awaiting PCB licence)
WADA plant phase 2 infrastructure built for up to ₹400 crore revenue by adding machines (no timeline given)

growth.why: Management targets FY27 revenue of about ₹800 crore (~17% over FY26's ₹684 crore) and EBITDA of ₹75-80 crore, backed by installed capacity up 22% to 76,931 MTPA, utilisation of 69% rising toward 80%, and a 5,000 MTPA recycling plant nearing licence; no order book was cited and capacity expansion is largely complete.
